title: The Politics of the NBA Finals
author: Daniel Falcone
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/marius-
christensen-_Ghzg0xvHW0-unsplash-680x453.jpg)

Image by Marius Christensen.

Aside from basketball, this year’s NBA Finals showcased civic identity and
political power. [Shea Serrano](https://x.com/SheaSerrano?s=20), author of
[_Expensive
Basketball_](https://www.npr.org/2025/10/29/nx-s1-5396832/expensive-
basketball-highlights-some-of-the-games-legendary-players-and-moments), once
argued that data is outweighed by the unquantifiable. Basketball can be
explained in the aesthetic, shared memory, or even the hidden statistic. For
example, [Sue Bird’s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_Bird) backpedal, [Tim
Duncan’s](https://www.theringer.com/2021/05/14/nba/tim-duncan-hall-of-fame-
spurs) dominance, or [Dwyane
Wade’s](https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/miamiheat/post/_/id/19125/inside-
dwyane-wades-all-time-blocks-mark) total in blocked shots (885 — the most ever
for a player 6:4 and under), all captured something beyond the numbers. Beyond
this, pure analytics certainly matter. The World Champion New York Knicks of
the 2026 NBA Finals topped the San Antonio Spurs in [True Shooting
Percentage](https://www.breakthroughbasketball.com/stats/tsp_calc), [Points
Per Possession](https://www.nbastuffer.com/analytics101/points-per-possession-
ppp/), and a higher [Value Over Replacement
Player](https://www.samford.edu/sports-analytics/fans/2023/The-Numbers-Dont-
Lie). Serrano’s methodology does not discount these tangibles but rather looks
at the significance of the abstract. And although the Knicks set records for
post-season wins and margins of victory, the team had obvious intangibles that
the Spurs failed to match. Basketball cannot be reduced to numbers, and
neither can the Knicks’ professional and social success story.

Journalist [Ari Paul](https://thebattleground.eu/author/arippaul/) recently
said that with the Knicks, “there’s a sense of thrill and connectedness I
haven’t felt in some time.” As something changed in the air, he referenced how
basketball was in the lifeblood of the city’s parks, schools, and YMCAs. Even
for fans that don’t play it, or follow it closely, it carries an omnipotent
pulse. Paul further stated, “too often on the political left, [pro-sports are
dismissed](https://www.economist.com/united-states/2026/06/11/the-knicks-
represent-new-york-and-capitalism-at-its-best) as [bread and
circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_and_circuses), [but] you don’t
even need to like basketball to see how the Knicks are lifting a kind of New
York City ‘patriotism’ that crosses class, race, and gender lines.”
International relations scholar [Stephen
Zunes](https://www.usfca.edu/faculty/stephen-zunes) commented, “seeing reels
of fans in bars and on the streets celebrating the Knicks’ winning the NBA
championship is a reminder of how delightfully racially and ethnically mixed
New York City is — which is why the rightwing hates it so much.”

Unfortunately, the victory was met by some with an uncomradely reaction;
resulting in widespread and wanton destruction.

When Knicks owner [James
Dolan](https://www.democracynow.org/2026/6/9/dave_zirin_trump_sports_fifa_ufc)
and Commissioner Adam Silver welcomed Donald Trump to Madison Square Garden
for Game Three of the NBA Finals, Journalist [Dave
Zirin](https://www.thenation.com/article/society/knicks-finals-donald-trump/)
wrote that “it’s like having Bull Connor show up to the NAACP Image Award
because he’s a fan of Misty Copeland.” Trump has [trashed the
NBA](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2026/06/08/trump-nba-knicks-
spurs-finals-madison-square-garden/90403963007/) but still found the need to
attend. As soon as he entered the picture, risking a hostile reception, fans
were prohibited from having watch parties. After the [United States Secret
Service](https://www.secretservice.gov/) and New York Police Department were
called in to ramp up security, there was a return to civic enjoyment for the
remainder of the series. Even with democratizing watch parties, [Josh
Hart](https://x.com/nypostsports/status/2063809500960723416) bemoaned the
outrageous ticket prices that prevented generational fans from attending.
They’ve waited decades for this moment, he emphasized.

In a sports league designed for individual players to navigate domestic,
[social, economic, and racial justice advocacy](https://nul.org/news/nba-
paint-black-lives-matter-courts-restart), NBA management struggles in
distancing itself from human rights violators like
[Qatar](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7337359/2026/06/05/fiba-basketball-
world-cup-2027-qatar-iran-war/), the [UAE](https://pr.nba.com/nba-and-
department-of-culture-and-tourism-abu-dhabi-announce-long-term-renewal-to-
bring-more-nba-games-and-activities-to-uae/),
[Israel](https://www.thenation.com/article/society/lebron-james-israel/), and
the current
[regime](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026/06/09/basketball/nba/trump-
knicks-nba-finals/). As writer [Roane
Carey](https://www.thenation.com/authors/roane-carey/) pointed out, “everyone
needs to focus more on the UAE’s criminal role in so many different conflicts.
And it’s atrocious that they’ve bought so many different athletic teams to
[wash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportswashing) their image.”

All the while, Mayor [Zohran
Mamdani](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/playoffs/2026/06/08/zohran-
mamdani-knicks-spurs-nba-finals-nosebleeds/90468586007/) has tried to harness
the Knicks fandom to support his own form of progressive politics and cultural
soft power in New York. Zirin might argue that Mamdani has made it easier to
focus less on the team’s high society aura and more on [_The City
Game_](https://www.nebraskapress.unl.edu/bison-books/9780803259348/the-city-
game/), as he embarks on crafting the Knicks energy around a civically minded
ethos. For the Finals, the Knicks preserved the image of the [anti-
team](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/05/01/the-mets-as-the-peoples-team/)
and placed their own team culture above ego as they rebelled against the
prematurely anointed
[superstar](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7334724/2026/06/05/victor-
wembanyama-nba-star-nike-spurs-adam-silver/) of the Western Conference. The
NBA Finals has also shown Mamdani’s ability to utilize social media in his
favor. The team’s orange and blue colors serving as a backdrop,
[advertised](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/03/nyregion/mamdani-knicks-ad-
campaign.html) other progressive candidates like [Brad
Lander](https://x.com/bradlander/status/2063410452324069573), [Darializa Avila
Chevalier](https://www.amny.com/politics/ny-13-congress-primary-debate-
espaillat-chevalier-06042026/) and [Claire
Valdez](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N436aXOTjGc); all have important
messages, ranging from blocking billionaire election interference, the
abolition of ICE, and standing up to property speculation.

The [New York Liberty](https://community.nyliberty.com/) won the WNBA in 2024.
Although the Knicks might have a way to go in catching up to them — a WNBA
franchise ahead of the curve in
[queer](https://community.nyliberty.com/pride/) representation, codified
[social justice commitments](https://liberty.wnba.com/social-justice-
commitment-statement), and fights for labor rights — something about this
year’s Knicks feels authentic and grassroots. For example, long-time Knick
diehard and filmmaker Spike Lee wore a [keffiyeh](https://forward.com/fast-
forward/805408/spike-lee-kyrie-irving-wear-pro-palestinian-outfits-to-nba-all-
star-game-featuring-first-israeli-player/) patterned shirt in support of
Palestine at the NBA All-Star game. It proved too much for a league tied
tightly to [American power](https://www.e-ir.info/2021/08/01/the-nba-and-the-
worlds-america/). Karl-Anthony Towns plays a key role in voting rights
restoration and serves on the board of the [Social Justice
Coalition](https://coalition.nba.com/). He was named the [Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
Social Justice Champion](https://www.basketball-
reference.com/awards/social_justice.html) in 2024 and even further, was
awarded the [Bob Lanier Community Assist](https://cares.nba.com/programs/nba-
cares-community-assist-award/) for helping to fund a sports facility in the
Dominican Republic. [Jalen Brunson](https://www.covenanthouse.org/news/jalen-
brunson-living-his-promise) serves as an ambassador for [Covenant
House](https://heckscherfoundation.org/grantee/covenant-house-new-
york/?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=12017152711&gbraid=0AAAAABtRDDe2LZvplH2QANAIOXYsXKvtA&gclid=CjwKCAjw857RBhAgEiwAI-1yKNhcxPtLVHY4DZH71PDqiqYAs0ed35ifKvpfSqm3jlDICpy12AlPrxoC64UQAvD_BwE),
dedicated to serving unhoused youth in New York City.

In some ways, the Knicks and Spurs could not be more different. The Knicks are
a large market in the north with gritty [Philly college
ball](https://www.vuhoops.com/general/34242/nova-knicks-nba-finals-
game-3-open-thread) players and a
[celebrity](https://www.townandcountrymag.com/leisure/sporting/a71527096/knicks-
game-3-nba-finals-2026-celebrities-photos/) entourage and legendary
[emeriti](https://andscape.com/features/new-york-knicks-alumni-finals-seats-
frazier-ewing-starks/). The Spurs are a smaller market, built around the
[fundamentals](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jbg6s3Yof2g), [corporate
knowledge](https://bleav.com/shows/small-market-bias-a-san-antonio-
spurs/episodes/corporate-knowledge-after-dark-spurs-vegas-vacation/), and an
international and generational
[talent](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/jun/01/victor-wembanyama-san-
antonio-spurs-nba-finals). The Spurs are not guided by a motivational culture
but an [operational](https://avnishanand-49235.medium.com/what-organisations-
can-learn-from-the-san-antonio-spurs-33b9b5da95e1) one. But it is apparent
that the Knicks inverted this script almost entirely.

But like the Knicks, the Spurs also have strong ties to progressive politics
and are members of [civil society](https://www.unesco.org/en/query-
list/c/civil-society). They participate in [PeacePlayers
International](https://peaceplayers.org/how-we-create-change/) to bridge
global divides at every [level of
society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level_of_analysis). Their team and
organization, from the top down, have spoken on the tragedies surrounding
[Palestine](https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1575668/gregg-popovich-our-
hearts-die-when-we-see-hamas-horror-and-bombs-killing-children-in-palestine/).
[Stephon Castle](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7233488/2026/04/26/deni-
avdija-stephon-castle-altercation-spurs-trail-blazers-playoffs-nba/) even
supplied vocal support for Gaza during live action. Further, the “[Spurs
nuns](https://sojo.net/articles/culture-interview/san-antonio-nuns-chanting-
go-spurs-go-and-god-bless)” of the Salesian order, educate disadvantaged youth
and have followed Spurs basketball on the Westside of San Antonio at the St.
John Bosco School since the 1990s. The Spurs’ organizational culture
[holistically develops](https://www.leagueoffans.org/2017/01/09/most-
progressive-coach-in-pro-sports-the-spurs-gregg-popovich/) coaches, athletes
and people. The previous Head Coach, Gregg Popovich was the first NBA coach to
hire a full-time woman assistant in the league, [Becky
Hammon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becky_Hammon). He also widely praised
[Colin Kaepernick’s](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27383352/popovich-
kaepernick-did-very-patriotic-thing) national anthem protests and opposes the
fascism of the Trump Administration.

As a former assistant with the Spurs, [Knicks Head Coach Mike
Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Brown_\(basketball,_born_1970\))
learned to prioritize individual needs. When Brown and his wife separated in
2002, [Popovich](https://nypost.com/2026/06/07/sports/how-gregg-popovich-
helped-knicks-mike-brown-arrive-at-this-moment/) insisted he not travel but
stay home with his sons. In a short time, Brown has helped Brunson develop
even more as a leader. Brunson provided the team with hope while defining
their reality. Moreover, Brown empowered his assistants and gave them a voice.
In two instances, assistants [Rick
Brunson](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZJm4UfiX2K/) and [Jordan
Brink](https://nypost.com/2026/06/06/sports/how-little-known-assistant-saved-
knicks-from-crushing-collapse/) were difference makers in post-season
outcomes.

Not since [1973](https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1973-nba-
finals-knicks-vs-lakers.html) had the [Knicks won a
title](https://x.com/gchiesaohmy/status/2066128393897418923?s=20). Even though
they remained a classic underdog, they were the more experienced,
[deeper](https://asaptext.com/orgs/nbafinals/browse_file.php?browse_file_name=transcripts/168292.html),
talented, and [tougher](https://nypost.com/2026/06/14/sports/mitchell-
robinson-has-his-long-awaited-knicks-forever-moment/) team. Aside from the
Finals drought, [Madison Square Garden](https://www.msg.com/madison-square-
garden/history), opening in
[1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden), has been a sports
and entertainment mecca. It was a site of hard luck despite its enduring
presence and unlike most stadiums, is a place of true urban integration. The
“neighborhood [walk-
to](https://stadiumandarenavisits.com/visitsreviews/95-madison-square-garden/)
arena” is a blessing in an era where outskirt stadium infrastructure models
stretch fan bases further from their central hubs.

In effect, [Mikal
Bridges](https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/mikal-bridges-
knicks-nba-title-rcx5nt19) and [OG
Anunoby](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3934719/og-anunoby) outplayed
the young Spurs squad with their own version of the ball-controlled “[Spurs
way](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-spurs-way-
podcast/id1282141288),” while valuing possessions and securing nearly every
50/50 loose ball. Victor Wembanyama struggled on the world stage when fatigue
became a factor.
[Brown](https://asaptext.com/orgs/nbafinals/transcripts/168235.pdf) outcoached
Spurs Head Coach [Mitch
Johnson](https://asaptext.com/orgs/nbafinals/transcripts/168234.pdf) and as
Tim Legler stated, the best adjustment a coach can make is a substitution. The
Spurs have famously asserted that it takes a player at least an entire season
to learn their system with overseas players learning it much faster. In this
contest, however, they might have taken a step backwards. Knicks starters and
[reserves](https://asaptext.com/orgs/nbafinals/transcripts/168418.pdf)
competed in a way San Antonio historically found familiar; by using the
[bench](https://nypost.com/2026/06/09/sports/knicks-get-unexpected-jordan-
clarkson-contribution-as-bench-thrives-in-nba-finals/), [shrinking the
court](https://www.scribd.com/document/701429379/NBA-Coaches-Clinic-
Notes-2011), and [allowing no middle dribble
penetration](https://x.com/TheHoopHerald/status/2063465241690677371?s=20),
second shots, or rebounding. Defensively, Tom Thibodeau’s handprints were
still all over the Knicks’ half court effort, while [Brown’s offensive
approach](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kf6E75Prl0I)
([“sprays”](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7339287/2026/06/07/knicks-sprays-
mike-brown-spurs-defense/)) were a [marked
improvement](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nafkpqunJOk) in terms of [spacing
and execution](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7cQCb9YkjcI).

Fans questioned whether the league seemingly selected officials more likely to
extend the series despite [Keldon
Johnson](https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/what-spurs-keldon-
johnson-say-playoff-struggles-22304717.php) and [De’Aaron
Fox’s](https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/spurs-offseason-preview-nba-finals-
loss-knicks-victor-wembanyama-deaaron-fox/) apparent disinterest in that
effort. Nonetheless, the Knicks excelled in floor balance and capitalized on
[rule changes that have made the NBA more perimeter and television
oriented](https://thesportjournal.org/article/the-impact-of-nba-new-rules-on-
games/). In the NBA, the two hardest things to guard are the early push and
second shots, according to Jeff Van Gundy. The Knicks outperformed in both. On
the Saturday practice [before Game
Three](https://asaptext.com/orgs/nbafinals/transcripts/168232.pdf), there was
footage of Rick Brunson calling his son over to speak with Patrick Ewing at
the Knicks shootaround. Brunson ran to
[Ewing](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZS-vliMBUM/). One of [Jay
Wright’s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lXqA6YkgMCg) key principles at
[Villanova](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/07/us/knicks-pope-leo-
villanova.html) was: “players never walk when on the court; there must be a
sense of urgency in everything you do.” In short, especially for [the Finals
MVP](https://jacobin.com/2026/06/nba-knicks-dolan-public-ownership), the
significance of these Finals was never confined to just basketball, as the
Knicks and Spurs provide a vehicle for civic belonging in an age of autocracy.

The post [The Politics of the NBA
Finals](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/06/15/the-politics-of-the-nba-
finals/) appeared first on [CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
